chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Matt al-Jawhari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran, who said: I was in Fayd when Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Bilal said, 'Let us go to the grave of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazī'. So we went to his grave, and Muhammad ibn 'Ali said: The owner of this grave narrated to me from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), that he said:
Whoever visits the grave of his believing brother, faces the Qiblah, places his hand on the grave, and recites 'Innā Anzalnāh' seven times, will be safe from the Great Terror.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended ritual and reward for visiting a believer's grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the intercessory merit of visiting a fellow believer's grave, a practice deeply rooted in Shia piety as an extension of the Prophet's tradition. The specific ritual of facing the Qiblah and reciting Surah Al-Qadr seven times is believed to secure deliverance from the 'Great Terror' (Al-Faz' al-Akbar) during the final resurrection, emphasizing the spiritual bond between the living and the deceased.
